🍟 snack maxxers · des 198 project 1

find it before you're hangry

Students open Snackpass but can't find what to eat. We added a filter button and a more visible search bar.

Team
Snack Maxxers: Coco, Nikolai, Qwyen, Terry, Janus
Timeline
October 1 – 29, 2026
Research
32 survey responses, 8 interviews
Tools
Figma, Google Forms, interviews

1 / 9 · overview

students stick to what they know because finding something new takes too long

Snackpass is the pickup app most Berkeley students use for drinks and quick meals. Searching for a place you already know works fine. But there's no way to ask "what boba is close and on sale right now?", so students reorder from the same few places. We added a filter button (cuisine, price, discounts, distance, and availability) and moved the search bar back to the top of the screen.

3 / 9 · core flows

from craving to order without knowing a store name

"I want something specific, wherever has it."

open app→tap filter→pick cuisine, price, discounts, distance→show results→order

"I don't know what I want yet."

open app→tap search→pick a craving (boba, sushi, korean bbq…)→order

"I know exactly where I'm going."

open app→search bar at the top→type the store→order

4 / 9 · research

7 of 8 people we interviewed pick food by how close it is

We surveyed 32 Berkeley students and interviewed 8 more about the last time they ordered food.

what students asked for

Show all open places
23
Discounts tab
21
Food/drink filters
15
More visible search bar
9

"Which feature would most improve your Snackpass experience?" n = 32. People could pick more than one.

what surprised us

  • Unhappy users still order a lot. They just don't explore. 6 of the 7 people who were dissatisfied with the layout order a few times a week or more, but 5 of those 7 rarely or never try new places. Among satisfied users it's 7 of 25.
  • 29 of 32 found it easy or moderately easy to find a store, so we didn't want to add features that clutter the page.
  • Distance decides. 7 of 8 interviewees named distance or location as what makes them pick a place.
  • Other apps win on delivery and flex dollars. 4 of 8 switch to Uber Eats or DoorDash when they want delivery, and 3 of 8 use Grubhub because it takes flex dollars.

in their words

Discounts and distance are also major factors that help me choose what to purchase.2nd year, mostly orders drinks
I'm not really a discount person. I think it is more so what's familiar and based on feelings.3rd year, orders about 3 times a week
I don't have a lot of pain points with it cuz I know what's on it and what isn't. I don't really use it as a food discovery app.3rd year, orders about 3 times a week
Genuinely difficult to find new places via Snackpass (you have to have an exact name in mind).Survey response, daily user

5 / 9 · explorations

we dropped the discounts tab students asked for

DroppedA "discounts" tab in the bottom bar21 of 32 asked for it. But it adds a fifth tab, and some of the people we interviewed don't order by deals at all.
KeptPromotions as one filter optionDeal-hunters get it in one tap, and nobody else sees extra clutter.

6 / 9 · prototyping & testing

both testers went straight for the filters, for discounts and price

We showed the Figma prototype to 2 students and asked for their honest reactions.

Having filters adds much more accessibility for me. Being able to filter by discounts or genre of food is really helpful when sometimes I don't want to see everything at once or if I want to save money.Tester 1
I like how the search bar is right at the top now, it's way easier to find stuff. Also the filters are really nice, especially being able to sort by price and distance, and having the ratings and discounts right there is super helpful too!Tester 2

what this does and doesn't tell us

  • Confirmed: both testers named the filters, and specifically saving money. That matches the survey, where 21 of 32 asked for discounts.
  • Not yet tested: we collected reactions, not tasks, so we didn't see anyone get stuck. Two people liking it is a good sign, but it isn't proof the filter button is easy to find.

7 / 9 · design decisions

three choices, each with what we turned down

One filter for cravings, deals, and distance

Students choose by craving, deals, and how far they'll walk, so the filter covers cuisine, price, discounts, distance, and availability in one sheet. It's especially useful when one store is closed but another one has what you want.

We moved the search bar back to the top

On Android, a glitch puts the "rate this store" card in front of the search bar, so people can't search for stores at all.

Promotions as a filter, not a separate tab

We turned down a "discounts" tab in the bottom bar. A filter keeps the main page uncluttered, especially for users who don't order based on discounts.

8 / 9 · constraints

what we didn't have

  • Time: three weeks.
  • Responses: 32 survey responses instead of our goal of 50.
  • Skill: our first time in Figma.

9 / 9 · reflections

next time, we'd watch people use the app

  • Get more data on exactly where people's pain points are.
  • Run in-person interviews where the person goes through Snackpass looking for something while we watch.
  • What we'd redo: survey an even number of students from each year, to see whether year changes how people use the app.
  • Where we used AI: we used AI to build our website so we could focus on writing and organizing our research. add anything else you used AI for
